Grow
GROH
v.
Old English growan, “to grow, increase, flourish.” Renders the Greek auxanō, “to grow, increase,” and the Hebrew gādal, “to grow great, become strong.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Growth, in Scripture, is the appointed pattern of every living thing God has made and especially of the regenerate soul, whose life is a maturing in grace and in the knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ. Peter sets the keynote command: but grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ; Paul prays for the Colossians that they may be increasing in the knowledge of God; the Ephesian believers are to grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ; the newborn babes are to desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. Growth is therefore not optional Christianity; it is the ordinary mark of regenerate life, as much as the growth of a healthy child is the mark of natural life. The patterns of biblical growth are several. There is growth in grace (the increasing experience of God’s favor and the increasing operation of His Spirit). There is growth in knowledge (the increasing apprehension of the doctrines of the faith and the person and work of Christ). There is growth in holiness (the increasing mortification of indwelling sin and the increasing vivification of the new man). There is growth in love (the increasing capacity for both the love of God and the love of neighbor). There is growth in usefulness (the increasing service rendered to the body and the world). And there is growth in likeness to Christ—the great end of all the other growths—until the saint at last attains, in the resurrection, the full measure of conformity to His glorified image. Growth happens by the appointed means: the Word (sincere milk, then strong meat), the sacraments, prayer, the assembling of the saints, the discipline of obedience, the providences of God by which the saint is exercised, and the indwelling Spirit who applies all the means. Growth has its seasons: rapid early growth at conversion, the long steady growth of mid-life, the deepening growth of the latter years; and its setbacks: dry seasons, fall-back, the necessary pruning by the Husbandman that prepares for fresh fruitfulness. To be a Christian is to be a growing thing; the unchanged believer at fifty whose grace, knowledge, holiness, love, and usefulness are no greater than at conversion is the most serious pastoral concern Scripture knows.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines GROW as to increase in size or stature, by a natural and insensible addition of matter, through nutrition; to enlarge; to extend; in scripture, to advance in moral or religious life; to make progress in grace.

expand to see more

GROW, v.i. — 1. To increase in size or stature, by a natural and insensible addition of matter, through nutrition. 2. To be augmented in size by accretion or addition of matter. 3. To advance; to make progress; to improve. Grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (2 Pet 3:18). 4. To increase in degree; to be augmented; as, vegetables grow ripe; pride grows offensive.

GROWING, ppr. — Increasing in bulk or stature; advancing; making progress.

📖 Key Scripture

2 Peter 3:18 — "But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen."

Ephesians 4:15 — "But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ."

1 Peter 2:2 — "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby."

Colossians 1:10 — "That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Growth is corrupted by the static-conversion register that treats the new birth as the whole story and growth as an optional extra—and by the inverse register that frenetically pursues every new spiritual technique and program without the patient ordinary-means growth Scripture actually describes.

expand to see more

Much of contemporary evangelicalism treats conversion as the whole Christian story: the sinner’s prayer is prayed, the decision is registered, the new birth is announced, and the work is essentially complete; subsequent growth in grace is an optional extra for the unusually serious. Scripture knows nothing of this static Christianity. The new birth is the beginning; growth is the appointed pattern of the regenerate life; the unchanged believer at fifty whose grace, knowledge, holiness, love, and usefulness are no greater than at conversion is the most serious pastoral concern Scripture knows. The recovery is the recovery of growth as ordinary and expected: every believer is to be growing, every season is to leave its mark on the soul, every providence is to be the means of some increase, every Sunday a small step forward in grace and the knowledge of Christ.

The opposite corruption is the frenetic pursuit of every new spiritual technique, program, conference, retreat, breakthrough method, deliverance ministry, or charismatic intensification, on the assumption that ordinary growth is too slow and what the soul needs is a shortcut to maturity. Scripture provides no such shortcut. Growth is by appointed means—the Word, the sacraments, prayer, the assembled saints, the disciplines of obedience, and the providences of God—applied patiently across years. The newborn babe grows by milk and the mature by strong meat; the branch grows by abiding in the Vine; the tree planted by the rivers of water brings forth its fruit in its season. The cure for slow growth is not a new program; it is the patient, faithful, ordinary use of the means God has appointed, sustained over the long years that growth in Christ actually requires.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek auxanō (to grow, increase) and Hebrew gādal (to grow great)—the appointed pattern of the regenerate life by the ordinary means God has provided, across the long years that maturity in Christ actually requires.

expand to see more

Greek auxanō (G837) — to grow, increase (1 Pet 2:2; 2 Pet 3:18; Eph 4:15; Col 1:6, 10; 2:19).

Greek auxesis (G838) — growth, increase (Eph 4:16; Col 2:19).

Hebrew gādal (H1431) — to grow great, become strong, magnify.

Greek prokoptō (G4298) — to advance, make progress (Luke 2:52, of Christ’s growth).
